extracted.intended_audience: editors, publishers, and distributors of historical journals / Project Gutenberg users
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for compiling and editing explorers' journals into a readable narrative while preserving documentary value, plus the Project Gutenberg license requirements for distributing the resulting eBook. Covers editorial principles (preservation, supplementation, format) and legal/redistribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original errors and note them
rubrics_metrics.description: [Errors in the original have been preserved and noted at the end of this etext.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing an edition compiled from original journals, retain original typographical or textual errors but explicitly note them for readers (e.g., list preserved errors at end of the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Render descriptions almost in original words
rubrics_metrics.description: In every case rendering the descriptions of the prominent incidents of the journey almost in the original words of the writers, merely adding as much as would save the text from abruptness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit editorial rewriting: keep description close to authors' original phrasing and only add minimal text to smooth abrupt transitions or clarify context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overuse editorial imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor, without drawing too much on his imagination, has, in the compilation of the journals, attempted in some cases to supplement what was wanted in the text...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement the primary text sparingly; avoid inventing scenes or facts. Any additions should be conservative, clearly editorial, and intended only to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to diurnal (daily) form for record value
rubrics_metrics.description: He has adhered to the diurnal form of narrative, for the sake of recording, for the benefit of future travellers, the numbers, marks, latitude, etc., of each camp...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the original daily/log form (dates, camp numbers, coordinates, marks) so the work retains practical value as a record for future travellers and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance documentary detail with narrative interest
rubrics_metrics.description: To the general reader, the usual monotonous details and entries of an explorer's notes, which alone give them value to the geographer, cannot be hoped to excite interest ... the Editor has attempted to put before the public a compilation of their journals in such form as will give the narrative sufficient interest to carry with it the attention of the reader to the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should strike a balance: keep geographers' detailed data for record value, while shaping or supplementing material to create a readable narrative for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include scientific/generic names for flora and fauna
rubrics_metrics.description: Aided by Mr. Jardine, senior ... the Editor has been enabled to supply the generic names of the birds and plants met with;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, provide scientific (generic) names for species mentioned to assist in identifying range, habitat, and for scientific value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use actors' graphic descriptions when no illustrations exist
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to be regretted that there was no one in the party having sufficient knowledge of drawing ... As these can now only be supplied from the graphic descriptions given by the actors in them, the Editor ... has, in the compilation of the journals, attempted in some cases to supplement what was wanted in the text, so as to give the narrative such color...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no visual plates or drawings are available, use vivid first-hand descriptions from participants to convey scenes; avoid inventing visual details beyond those described by eyewitnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain authenticity and modest editorial presence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Brothers Jardine themselves would probably much rather repeat their journey than write a full account of it ... it has devolved on the Editor to attempt to put before the public a compilation of their journals in such form as will give the narrative sufficient interest ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect original authors' voice and humility; keep editorial voice secondary and transparent, especially when authors preferred not to 'go into print'.
